answer.rationale: Write latency climbing 5x during settlement peak with heavy transactional load suggests resource contention on the write path. The security patch cannot be reverted per compliance. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect against dependency failures but won't address capacity-driven latency. Provisioning headroom during peaks (memory_b3) has proven effective for absorbing surge traffic without customer impact. Adding capacity targets the root cause directly while preserving the mandatory security patch. This maintains the primary objective of sustained availability without reverting writes.
